overview: The Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act concerns Wintergreen, a mountain resort community in Virginia next to the Blue Ridge Parkway, a scenic road run by the National Park Service. It requires the Interior Department to grant a right-of-way, meaning legal permission to cross federal land, for an emergency exit road shown on a 2024 map near milepost 9.6 of the parkway. Before granting it, the department must report to Congress that it has studied alternatives that avoid federal land, including converting existing trails into roads, analyzed how wildfire would behave along the route, and finished any required environmental and historic preservation reviews. As of September 23, 2026, a Senate committee had approved an amended version and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say residents and visitors need a second way out in a wildfire or other emergency, and the bill makes sure that route can be built once safety and environmental reviews are done.
against: Critics say requiring the government to grant access across national parkland sets a precedent for private needs to override park protections, though the bill does require alternatives to be studied first.
